description: Paya Soup is a rich, gelatinous, and highly flavorful Pakistani delicacy made from trotters. Slow-cooked to perfection with aromatic spices, it offers a deeply comforting and nourishing experience. This hearty soup is often enjoyed for breakfast or as a special occasion meal, renowned for its distinct taste and health benefits.

instructions.title: Prepare the Paya
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the goat or lamb trotters under running water. If not already done by your butcher, singe off any remaining hair over an open flame and scrape clean. Rinse several times until the water runs clear. Set aside to drain.

instructions.title: Brown Aromatics
instructions.text: In a pressure cooker, heat the cooking oil over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and fry until they turn golden brown. Ensure even browning to develop a rich flavor for the soup.

instructions.title: Sauté Spices and Paya
instructions.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste to the browned onions and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, salt, black peppercorns, green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for another 2 minutes, stirring continuously. Add the cleaned paya and sauté for 5 minutes, ensuring they are well coated with the spices.

instructions.title: Pressure Cook the Paya
instructions.text: Pour in 6-8 cups of water, enough to submerge the paya completely. Close the pressure cooker lid and cook on high heat until the first whistle, then reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 20-25 minutes. This duration is for relatively small, tender paya. Allow the pressure to release naturally before opening the lid.

instructions.title: Check Tenderness and Adjust Consistency
instructions.text: Once the pressure is released, carefully open the lid. Check if the paya are tender and falling off the bone. If not, cook for another 10-15 minutes under pressure or simmer on low heat until desired tenderness is achieved. Stir in the garam masala powder. If the soup is too thin, you can simmer it uncovered for a few minutes to reduce. If too thick, add a little hot water.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Taste and adjust salt if necessary. Ladle the hot Paya Soup into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh julienned ginger, chopped fresh coriander, and sliced green chilies. Serve immediately with hot naan, tandoori roti, or plain rice for a truly authentic Pakistani meal.

tips: For truly tender paya in a pressure cooker, ensure small, well-cut pieces. If using a regular pot, simmer for 3-4 hours on low heat until the meat is falling off the bone.
To enhance the flavor profile, add a pinch of star anise and black cumin (shahi zeera) along with other whole spices during the sautéing stage.
Paya Soup often tastes even better the next day as the flavors develop. Reheat gently on low heat, adding a little water if needed to adjust consistency, and always garnish fresh before serving.
